extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent applicants and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how an examiner may issue a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, and how applicants must reply. Covers the kinds of information that may be required, timing, format, reply completeness, examiner obligations, and related procedures (IDS, petitions, timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: (H) Reply to matter raised in a protest under 37 CFR 1.291
rubrics_metrics.description: (H) A reply to a matter raised in a protest under 37 CFR 1.291.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require applicant to reply to protest issues disclosed under 1.291 as part of a 1.105 requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: (I) Explanation of technical material in a publication
rubrics_metrics.description: (I) An explanation of technical material in a publication, such as one of the inventor's publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be required to explain technical content in publications referenced in the file to clarify relevance or meaning to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: (J) Identification of changes in a reformatted continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: (J) The identification of changes made in a reformatted continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require applicant to identify what was changed in a reformatted continuing application to facilitate examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: (K) Mark-up for continuation-in-part showing added subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: (K) A mark-up for a continuation-in-part application showing the subject matter added where there is an intervening reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may request mark-ups to identify new subject matter in CIPs particularly when intervening references exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: (L) Comments on a new Federal Circuit decision
rubrics_metrics.description: (L) Comments on a new decision by the Federal Circuit that appears on point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be required to comment on newly-published controlling case law that affects patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: (M) Publication date of an undated document mentioned by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: (M) The publication date of an undated document mentioned by applicant that may qualify as printed publication prior art (35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an undated document is invoked, examiner can require verification of publication date to assess prior art status.

rubrics_metrics.name: (N) Comments on potential derivation under 35 U.S.C. 102(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: (N) Comments on information of record which raises a question of whether applicant derived the invention from another under 35 U.S.C. 102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may seek factual input from applicant where derivation issues appear on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: (O) Art related to applicant's invention or disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: (O) Art related to applicant's invention, applicant's disclosure, or the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require applicant to identify art that is related to the claimed subject matter or disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: (P) Other factual information pertinent to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: (P) Other factual information pertinent to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for other factual matters the examiner reasonably deems necessary to assess patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Q) Accuracy of the examiner's stated analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: (Q) The accuracy of the examiner's stated analysis of such items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be asked to correct or clarify inaccuracies in the examiner's analysis of facts or references.

rubrics_metrics.name: (R) Clarification for means/steps-plus-function support
rubrics_metrics.description: (R) Clarification of the correlation and identification of what structure, material, or acts set forth in the specification would be capable of carrying out a function recited in a means or steps plus function claim limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If support for such claim limitations is not apparent and applicant cannot identify it, examiner may conclude lack of support and make rejections (e.g., under 35 U.S.C. 112). Applicant should be asked to point to specific spec/drawings pages/lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S) Use of interrogatories or stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: (S) Interrogatories or Stipulations to elicit facts known to applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require agreement/disagreement to stipulated facts or answers to interrogatories to clarify the record about uncontroverted matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(1) Common technical features among claims / admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(1) Of the common technical features shared among all claims, or admission that certain groups of claims do not share any common technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine claim grouping, unity, or claim correspondence for examination and restriction purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(2) Support for means/steps-plus-function claims (35 U.S.C. 112, ¶6)
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(2) About the support found in the disclosure for means or steps plus function claims (35 U.S.C. 112, paragraph 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatory to identify where specification provides structure/acts corresponding to claimed functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(3) Which portions provide written description and enablement for specific claim elements
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(3) Of precisely which portion(s) of the disclosure provide the written description and enablement support for specific claim element(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should point to exact pages/lines illustrating support for each claim element to address 112 concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(4) Meaning of claim limitations / scope of terms
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(4) Of the meaning of claim limitations or terms used in the claims, such as what teachings in the prior art would be covered by particular limitations or terms in a claim and which dictionary definitions would define a particular claim term, particularly where those terms are not used per se in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to clarify claim language and scope; applicant may be asked to identify dictionary definitions or prior art teachings that correspond to claim terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(5) Which portions of each claim correspond to any admitted prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(5) Of which portions of each claim correspond to any admitted prior art in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps isolate novel claim aspects and assess obviousness/anticipation relative to admitted prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(6) Specific utility provided by the claimed subject matter on a claim-by-claim basis
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(6) Of the specific utility provided by the claimed subject matter on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should state what utility each claim provides to satisfy utility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(7) Whether dependent claim element is known in prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(7) As to whether a dependent claim element is known in the prior art based on the examiner having a reasonable basis for believing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be required to confirm whether dependent elements are novel or anticipated by prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(8) Support for added limitations in an amended claim
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(8) Of support for added limitations in an amended claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims are amended, applicant may need to identify where new limitations are supported in the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: (S)(9) Facts related to public use or sale situations
rubrics_metrics.description: (S)(9) Of facts related to public use or sale situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To evaluate potential statutory bars or prior public uses/sales, examiner can ask for factual details from applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary timing: when a 1.105 requirement may be made
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 is discretionary and may be made at any time once the necessity for it is recognized; optimum time is prior to or with a first action on the merits because the examiner has the maximum opportunity to consider and apply the response. Ordinarily, a request for information should not be made with or after a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should make the requirement at the earliest opportunity after recognizing necessity; avoid making it with/after final rejection except in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors supporting requirement prior to first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to consider for appropriateness of a separate requirement prior to first action include: (A) newly established art area without well-developed prior art resources; (B) whether applicant submitted an IDS; (C) whether specification's background adequately describes the background; (D) whether related documents by inventor/assignee not submitted are found during search; (E) whether non-patent literature is referred to but a copy not supplied; (F) whether background describes information as known/conventional that is unfamiliar and cannot be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these factors to determine whether a pre-first-action requirement is warranted to extend search/domain of art or obtain missing background information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness with first action on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement may be combined with a first action on the merits that includes at least one rejection if the application file or lack of relevant prior art found in the examiner’s search justifies asking the applicant for relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine requirement with a first-action allowance or Ex parte Quayle action based solely on lack of prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness after first action on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement made after the first action may be appropriate when the application file justifies asking the applicant for information relevant to patentability; it is rarely appropriate to require information because of lack of relevant prior art after the first action. A requirement is not proper when no further action would be taken by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because requirement implies further examiner action, it's generally used in non-final actions; limited circumstances allow requirements in issued/abandoned applications (e.g., revival, inventorship change, reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reply standard to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply is a reply to each enumerated requirement giving either the information required or a statement that the information required is unknown and/or is not readily available to the party or parties from which it was requested. Applicant must make a good faith attempt and reasonable inquiry to obtain the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant need not prove the information was unattainable; a truthful statement that it is unknown or not readily available is generally sufficient unless the reply is ambiguous or indicates misunderstanding. Follow-up requirement may be made if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to replies to 1.105 requirements: applicant must reply with information reasonably and readily available. The threshold for 1.56 (material to patentability) is substantially higher than the requirement for 1.105 (reasonable necessity to examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit information already known, but are not required to search for unknown information under 1.105. Examiners can require information that may not be material in itself but is necessary for a complete examination record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of incomplete replies
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply to a 1.105 requirement in a pending application or reexamination is handled as an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final Office action (see 37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP § 714.03). Where the reply is bona fide, form paragraph 7.95 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omission was deliberate or application is subject to final Office action, the examiner cannot grant an extension if reply period expired; use appropriate form paragraphs and give applicant opportunity (usually 1 month) to supply omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for reply and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to a 1.105 requirement are governed by 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136. Requirements made without an action on the merits should set a shortened statutory period of two months for reply; applicant may extend up to six months under 1.136(a). Requirements sent with an Office action have the same reply period as the action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply within the time results in abandonment. 1.105 requirements are Office actions under 35 U.S.C. 132 for patent term adjustment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: narrow scope and limited burden
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 1.105 should be narrowly specified and limited in scope because it is a significant burden on both applicant and the Office; it is warranted only where the benefit from the information exceeds the burden of obtaining it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully tailor the requirement to avoid inviting large volumes of irrelevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and content of the requirement (notice content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement must clearly indicate that a 1.105 requirement is being made, the basis for the requirement, and what information is being required. Requirements should specify the particular art area involved and the particular claimed subject matter within such art area, and indicate the form the required information is expected to take (citations/copies, identification of collections, answers to questions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare as a separate document (preferred) or attached to an Office action; state why the requirement was made and how the information is necessary to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interrogatories and stipulations (format options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories may be used to ask specific questions seeking applicant’s factual knowledge; stipulations may be used to request agreement or disagreement to factual assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each interrogatory/stipulation must be clearly set forth and characterized as factual information where appropriate; suggest formatting (e.g., append (agree/disagree)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and specific required-subject templates
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of form paragraphs (7.105 – 7.127 etc.) should be used when preparing a requirement, with tailored templates for domains such as domain of search, level of skill, background description, products embodying the invention, art suggested as relevant, list of keywords, citations for searchable databases, copies of art referred to but not submitted, copies of inventor-authored publications, art relied upon for prior art description/development/drafting, names of products incorporating claimed invention or prior art, details of improvement over prior art, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific form paragraph that matches the information sought; follow the examiner notes in each paragraph for how to populate bracketed fields and limitations on scope (many templates limit the requirement to documents actually relied on vs. merely relevant documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of fee and certification for initial replies
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 are waived for documents submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement if included in the applicant's first complete communication responding to the requirement. Supplemental replies after the first communication and any disclosures beyond the scope are subject to 1.97 fee/certification requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use waiver where applicable; instruct applicants to include a list of references (PTO/SB/08) to have citations entered in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a good faith reply (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply must be made with candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56. If the applicant does not have or cannot readily obtain an item, a statement that the item is unknown or cannot be readily obtained may be accepted as a complete reply for that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this reminder in the conclusion of any requirement for information and advise applicants about acceptable statements regarding unavailable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's obligation to consider and indicate consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must consider the information submitted and apply it as appropriate; indication of consideration must appear in the record (e.g., 'Considered' with initials/date). For art submitted, examiner must indicate which art was considered and which was not, if applicant provides a written list; if examiner relies on submitted art in a rejection, the art must be of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, follow IFW Manual; do not refuse to consider information within the scope of the requirement; if art is beyond scope, it need not be considered unless submitted per 1.97/1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope measurement principle (plain meaning of the text)
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for measuring the scope of a 1.105 requirement is the plain meaning of the text of the requirement; therefore, it is essential to carefully specify the scope of information required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrowly word the requirement to avoid submissions of irrelevant art and to make clear what will and will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to challenge a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to the Director of the Technology Center to have a requirement withdrawn or modified, or to have information submitted under 1.105 considered; however, a petition is not a reply and the time to reply to the 1.105 requirement continues to run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition does not stop the statutory reply period; applicants must still timely reply to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to Information Disclosure Statements (37 CFR 1.97/1.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial reply responsive to a 1.105 requirement and timely submitted does not have to satisfy the fee/certification of 1.97/1.98; applicant should list references on PTO/SB/08. Any submissions beyond the scope of the 1.105 requirement or any supplemental replies after the initial reply must comply with 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 609.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement within scope will be considered like IDS art; art beyond scope is treated as an IDS and must meet IDS rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on making a subsequent Office action final relying on submitted art
rubrics_metrics.description: Where information is submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of the application of such art are necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes post-1.105-reply practice from practice after a submission under 1.97/1.98; if examiner wants to rely on submitted art in a final action, ensure rejections are necessitated by applicant amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of only pertinent pages for large documents (¶ 7.122)
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding with copies of documents that are large (bound text or single article over 50 pages), the applicant may meet the requirement by providing copies of only those pages that provide the particular subject matter indicated in the requirement, or where not indicated, the subject matter found in applicant's disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to limit burden on applicants when large documents are involved; specify pertinent pages in requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph templates for conclusions and timing (¶ 7.125-7.127)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶ 7.125 when requirement accompanies an Office action (reply period coincides with action); use ¶ 7.126 when mailed without any other Office action (shortened statutory period of [1] months, ordinarily 2 months); use ¶ 7.127 to conclude an Office action that includes a requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate concluding form paragraph to set the correct reply period and to instruct applicants on timing and extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of applicant's prior art search (¶ 7.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response, applicant should state whether any search of prior art was performed; if performed, state citations for each prior art collection searched and list any art retrieved that was considered material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps examiner understand what the applicant already knows/has searched and may avoid redundant searching.
